newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends firmer on talk of frost next week.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends firmer on talk of frost next week.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firm on concerns about some forecasts for frost early next week in the northern portion of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"People didn't want to be short for the weekend and we'll see what happens Monday with the weather," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Several meteorologists early Friday cited the potential for frosty temperatures in northern Iowa, northern Illinois, southern Minnesota and southern Wisconsin.
Another more severe cold system was expected Sep 29-30.
Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, said these temperatures should produce scattered frosts in low-lying areas, but clouds or wind could limit the scope of the frost.

Fund demand was estimated at nearly 10.0 million bushels with R.J. O'Brien purchasing four million December and O'Connor and Co bought 4.5 million December, the traders said. Cargill Inc bull spread nine million Dec/Mar and ADM Investor Services spread five million March/December, they said.
Corn closed 3/4 to two cents per bushel higher, with December up 3/4 at $3.14-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 40,000, down from 52,344 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Smith Barney bought 1,200 May $3.60 calls at 9-1/4, sold 1,600 December $3.00 calls at 18-1/2 to 19 and bought 1,000 March $3.20 puts and sold 1,000 July $3.20 puts at 1-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Options volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 20,234 Thursday.
